author: adjudicator
time_standard: Gettysburg local mean time (LMT); witnesses wrote their own unsynchronised watch time, no conversion applied.
quote_check: Every quotation (under 15 words, OCR text of the Internet Archive scans of the 1889 GPO Official Records and the cited periodicals) was matched by script after folding case and punctuation against the full OCR text (tmp/clock-adj/vsrc.py). No page image was opened: an OCR slip in a figure is possible. Pages are the printed folio of the cited work as found in the OCR running heads.

1.note: Heth's report: the division was ordered to move at 5 a.m. (one witness; an order time, not a departure time).
1.resolution: Single report (OR 27/2 p. 637, written 13 Sep 1863). Window 04:45 to 05:30 because an order time is not a departure time and one witness cannot claim better than the 10 to 30 minute scatter between 1863 watches.

5.note: Derived from tick 1 and the column's length; not an independent datum (circular, kept as a design-class anchor).
5.resolution: Unchanged. The brigade order inside Heth's column is not timed in any source read; the anchor only keeps the pre-07:30 slope realistic and is labelled an estimate.

12.note: First shot about 07:30 rests on Lt. Jones's later account; the Official Records give 'about 8' for the notice that the enemy was coming.
12.resolution: Old window (07:30 exactly, 5 min) was narrower than any source supports. Gamble (about 8:00, OR 27/1 p. 934) and Buford (between 8 and 9, p. 927) time the reports that followed the shot, so the shot was at or before 08:00. 07:30 is kept as the value in the repo's earlier evidence (HistoryNet, Wikipedia, Lt. Jones's own later account, none of them read here as a primary text); it is an estimate with a window, not a documented minute.

28.note: Wadsworth and Doubleday (OR 27/1 pp. 266, 245): about 10.15. Sequence bounds 10.00 to 10.50 (Hunt 10.15 Reynolds alive; Hall opened 10.45).
28.resolution: Historians a and b agree on 10:15. Both Union generals may be one witness family (Doubleday may follow Wadsworth), so the window runs to the sequence bound (about 10:50). Howard's 11.15 and 11.30 are when the news arrived. The 'dispute 10:40-10:50' in the old note is not found in any primary text; it only equals the sequence bound.

36.note: No report clocks the Railroad Cut charge; sequence after Reynolds (10:15) and Hofmann's 'engaged at 11 a.m.'.
36.resolution: The old window (10:45 to 11:15) was narrower than the evidence: the Official Records describe the charge (Doubleday OR 27/1 p. 246) without a time. Bounds: after Reynolds fell (about 10:15) and Hall opened at 10:45; Hofmann (56th Pa., same brigade) engaged at 11:00.

53.note: Doubleday 13:30 (advance), Lee 14:30 (Rodes arrives), Howard 14:45 (enemy in force); Baxter engaged over two hours from about noon.
53.resolution: No report clocks the volley into Iverson's flank. The Union and Confederate clocks differ by up to an hour (Doubleday 1.30 vs Lee 2.30). 14:30 stays as the middle of 14:00 to 15:00.

57.note: Hays: Gordon ordered forward a little after 14:00; Howard first sees the enemy in force at 14:45 and the line is giving way by 15:45.
57.resolution: Window widened from 14:30-15:15 to 14:30-15:30: the Confederate order (a little after 14:00, plus the advance) and the Union sightings (14:45; giving way before 15:45) bracket the collapse of Barlow's Knoll. No report clocks the moment itself.

64.note: Doubleday 'About 4 p.m.' (general advance), Rowley 'nearly 4'; Howard puts a renewed attack on the I Corps at 15:20.
64.resolution: Window widened from 15:45-16:15 to 15:20-16:15 to include Howard's 3.20 (OR 27/1 p. 703); 16:00 stays (two reports).

72.note: Hancock's dispatch stamped 5.25 p.m.: arrived 'an hour since' (16:25); Howard the same day: 4 p.m. Hancock's later report says 3 p.m.
72.resolution: Two same-day written sources (16:00 and about 16:25) agree. Hancock's later report says 3 p.m. but its next sentences describe the I and XI Corps as already retiring through the town, which Howard dates from 4.10 p.m., so the 3 p.m. conflicts with the report's own sequence and is treated as a slip (window starts 15:30). A reader who prefers 15:00 would mark this anchor Contested; the adjudicator judges the sequence argument decisive.

75.note: NO source gives a clock time for Lee's order. Estimate from sequence: after the retreat (16:10 to 16:30) and before Hancock's 'quiet' dispatch (17:25).
75.resolution: Historians a and b both found no clock time (a: working value 16:45, window 16:15-17:30; b: no point, window 16:30-17:30, placeholder 16:55). The adjudicator searched the Official Records (Ewell, Early, Hays, Lee) and Taylor 1906 and Long 1886 and found none either. Value 16:55 is the centre of the union window 16:20-17:30 and lies between ticks 72 (16:20) and 90 (17:30). It is an estimate and must be shown with 'about'.

90.note: XII Corps: head near the field about 16:00 (Crane), Slocum 'coming on the ground' 17:25 (Hancock), Geary in position 17:00, Howard/Meade 'about 7'. Johnson (the Confederate half) about 19:00.
90.resolution: Historians: a 17:30 (16:00-19:00), b 17:25 (17:00-18:00). Adjudicator: Hancock's stamped note and report (17:00-18:00) are the best evidence for the corps arriving; the 16:00 and 19:00 readings are real primary statements about the column head and about the generals' meeting, so the displayed window stays 16:00-19:00 and the status is Contested. CONTENT: the card text puts the XII Corps on Culp's Hill that evening; Geary (OR 27/1 p. 825) went there at 5 a.m. on 2 July.

100.note: Design anchor (nightfall): sunset 19:32 to civil dusk 20:04 LMT, recomputed independently, agrees within 1 minute.
100.resolution: Not a historical event. Solar times recomputed with a second implementation of the NOAA/Meeus algorithm (docs/time/evidence/solar_check.py): sunset 19:32, civil dusk 20:04 or 20:05, nautical dusk 20:46. Not checked against a printed almanac.

226.note: Design anchor (Day 2 first light): civil dawn 04:03, sunrise 04:35 LMT.
226.resolution: Not a historical event; same independent solar check (civil dawn 04:02 to 04:03, sunrise 04:35).

240.note: Berdan: second detachment ordered about 11 a.m.; Hunt: sent about 12 m.; Birney: permission at 12 m. (1863) or 11 (1864 testimony).
240.resolution: Window widened from 11:30-12:30 to 11:00-12:30 because Berdan's own report and Birney's 1864 testimony say about 11:00. Noon stays (Hunt, Birney 1863).

248.note: The advance was in stages: announced 13:00-14:00 (Randolph), seen as an advance at 15:00 (Hancock, Meade), second division moved to the road about 16:00 (Humphreys, Meade's 1864 testimony).
248.resolution: Historians a and b agree: 15:00, window 14:00-16:00, CONTESTED (the 'start of the move' reading is 13:00-14:00). Adjudicator concurs and checked the quotations. The old 14:30 with range 12:00-15:30 is replaced.

256.note: Alexander, Pendleton, Bryan: about 16:00; Bane about 16:30.
256.resolution: Time and window unchanged. Alexander, Pendleton, Bryan and Longstreet agree on about 16:00, Bane on about 16:30; the window 15:45 to 16:30 contains all of them.

267.note: Rice, Conner: brigade placed about 16:00; Hunt: Hazlett to the hill about 16:30, after Vincent's brigade.
267.resolution: Window widened from 16:15-16:45 to 16:00-16:50. No report clocks the moment Vincent's brigade reached the summit; it is inferred from 'about 4' orders and the Hazlett time.

275.note: No participant clocks the charge. Chamberlain: about an hour of severe fighting after about 16:00-16:30; Woodward: enemy fell back nearly 18:00; Oates: his regiment broke and rallied about sunset (19:32).
275.resolution: Historians a and b agree: 18:00. Window: a 17:15-19:00, b 17:30-18:45. Adjudicator: lower edge 17:30 (the 17:10 and 17:15 readings have no support in the texts read); upper edge 19:00 kept because Oates is a first-hand source who places the aftermath at sunset. CONTESTED.

280.note: Hunt: the line was forced back 'about 5.30 or 6'; Lang: Wilcox began to advance 18:00; Wilcox: the cannonade lasted until 18:20.
280.resolution: Old anchor 18:30 (18:00-18:45) rested on a site marker; the reports centre on about 18:00-18:20. Moved to 18:15, window 17:45-18:45. Order after tick 275 (18:00) preserved.

295.note: No clock in Crawford's report ('as night was approaching'); sequence after the Peach Orchard fell (about 18:15) and before dusk.
295.resolution: Time and window unchanged. The evidence is sequence only: Crawford's report says the charge was made as night was approaching, and the Peach Orchard had fallen about 18:15; no report clocks the Pennsylvania Reserves' counterattack.

302.note: The Official Records describe the charge without a time; sequence after Wilcox began to advance (18:00-18:20) and before 'near dusk' (Humphreys).
302.resolution: Time unchanged, window 18:45 to 19:30. Hancock's report (OR 27/1) describes the charge with no clock; the bounds come from Wilcox's advance (18:00 to 18:20) and Humphreys's 'near dusk'.

314.note: Greene: attacked 'a few minutes before 7 p.m.'; Early: Johnson 'warmly engaged' before dusk (20:04).
314.resolution: Window widened to 18:50-19:45 so that both the Union clock (about 18:55) and Early's clock are inside. Time 19:20 kept.

326.note: Hays 'a little before 8', Early 'a little before dusk', Ricketts and Meade about 20:00, Schurz 20:00-21:00, Tate 'fully dark'.
326.resolution: Historians a and b agree. Applies to the East Cemetery Hill attack only; Johnson's Culp's Hill attack (tick 314) began about 19:00, so the Turning Points entry covering both should read 'evening, about 7 to 8:30 p.m.'.

340.note: Geary: Culp's Hill attack broken off about 22:00; Howard: line resumed 21:30; Steuart rested from about 23:00.
340.resolution: Old anchor 22:30 (22:00-22:30) excluded Howard's 21:30 and Steuart's 23:00. Moved to 22:15, window 21:30-23:00.

451.note: Slocum: XII Corps artillery opened at 4 a.m.; Hunt: Reserve batteries 4.30; Geary 3.30 (before civil dawn, so a fast watch); regimental reports 'about 4'.
451.resolution: Old anchor 04:30; the reports centre on about 04:00-04:30. Moved to 04:15, window 03:45-04:45. Tick 451 is the start of the third tab.

500.note: Peyton (Garnett's brigade): reached the field about 9 a.m. One witness.
500.resolution: Time unchanged. The old upper edge 10:00 had no source in the texts read (one brigade report; the other Pickett brigades filed none), so the window is trimmed to 08:30-09:30.

515.note: Slocum: engagement continued until 10.30; Hunt, Ruger: about 10; Geary, Hayes: about 11.
515.resolution: Old anchor 11:00 (10:30-12:00) was at the late edge. Moved to 10:30, window 10:00-11:15.

518.note: Nine reports on both sides say about 13:00; Alexander: 13:00 by his watch; Walton: Longstreet's order arrived a few minutes after 13:00; Peyton 13:30 (his watch).
518.resolution: Historians a and b: SUPPORTED at 'about 1 p.m.' (a 13:00, b 13:05). The minute 13:07 appears in no primary text read (only a magazine article, Welsh). Time set to 13:00. Uncertainty set to 30 minutes (half-width 25), not 10, because the witnesses' watches were not calibrated and the cluster includes Peyton 13:30 and Eshleman 'between 1 and 2'.

538.note: Webb, Hunt, Harrow (Union) and Davis (Confederate): about 15:00; Peyton 14:30 on a watch that gives 13:30 for the opening; Jones about 14:00; Alexander about 14:00.
538.resolution: Historians: a 14:45 (14:30-15:00), b 15:00 (14:00-15:15). Adjudicator: Webb's 'At 3 o'clock the enemy's line of battle left the woods' (OR 27/1 p. 429) adds a fourth first-hand statement at 15:00, so 15:00 stands (this is the existing anchor). The Confederate order times (14:00-14:30) are inside the window. CONTESTED.

551.note: No clock in Webb's report; sequence 20 to 35 minutes after the 15:00 step-off.
551.resolution: Window widened to 15:10-16:00 because tick 538 is Contested. Time unchanged.

556.note: Davis: Heth's division back on Seminary Ridge about 16:00; Lee's meeting with survivors is later and is not timed in the texts read.
556.resolution: Time and window unchanged. Davis (OR 27/2 p. 651) gives about 16:00 for Heth's division reaching its morning line; Lee's meeting with the survivors is not timed in any text read, so this anchor is an estimate.

568.note: Preston (1st Vt. Cav.): the charge at 5 p.m.; Capehart (1st W.Va.): contact at 3 p.m., order to make ready.
568.resolution: Time unchanged, window 16:45 to 17:45. Preston (OR 27/1 p. 1013) dates the charge 5 p.m.; Capehart (p. 1018) has the force in contact at 3 p.m. and Farnsworth told to make ready, so the charge itself is the later event; the window is one hour about Preston's figure.

675.note: Design anchor (nominal end of the battle): sunset to civil dusk, same solar check.
675.resolution: Not a historical event: the nominal end of the battle, set at civil dusk so that the third day has a closing frame.
